findings.title: Serialize index creation per resource key before publishing
findings.body: The cache mutex now protects only publication, so GetIndex returns nil while an index is being built. Concurrent searches, or a search and the write-event handler, can consequently build separate indexes for the same namespace/group/resource. For memory indexes, the last builder overwrites the cached index; an event applied to the other index can then be lost from subsequent search results. For file indexes, both builders attempt bleve.New on the same directory and one fails. Add per-key synchronization and recheck the cache after acquiring it, while retaining parallel builds for different keys.

findings.title: Preserve rejection of requests after Stop
findings.body: Removing the Init checks also removes the stopped-state check: Stop sets initErr to a stopping/stopped error, which previously caused subsequent RPCs to be rejected by Init. Create, Update, Delete and the other handlers now continue using the backend after Stop. In particular, the SQL backend's Stop only cancels its pollers, so writes can still succeed after shutdown while watchers and search indexing are no longer running. Preserve a separate lifecycle-state guard in the handlers rather than relying on eager initialization alone.
